files.relevance: changed; new use case whose swallowed gateway errors and commit ownership need review
changed; new repository whose flush-only write and untested get_latest need review
changed; new tests covering ChargeAccount but not ChargeRepository

key_patterns: Use cases take their collaborators through constructor injection (charge.py, ChargeAccount.__init__(gateway, repository)).
Request data crossing a use case boundary is a frozen dataclass (charge.py, ChargeRequest).
Repository writes call session.flush(), not commit, and no commit call is visible in this diff (repository.py, ChargeRepository.save).
New billing code is split into application/ and infrastructure/ under app/modules/billing/ (charge.py, repository.py paths).
Tests fake a use case's ports (gateway, repository) instead of hitting real infrastructure (tests/test_charge.py, FakeGateway/FakeRepository).
Async use cases and repository methods use pytest.mark.asyncio and async def throughout (tests/test_charge.py, charge.py, repository.py).
recommendations: Verify the `except Exception:` in ChargeAccount.execute (charge.py) logs or re-raises the failure instead of swallowing it (from: Error Handling Standards)
Confirm where the charge transaction commits: ChargeRepository.save (repository.py) only flushes, and charge.py shows no commit call (from: Clean Architecture Boundaries)
Check that no database transaction spans the gateway.charge() network call inside ChargeAccount.execute (charge.py) (from: Clean Architecture Boundaries)
Add or point to tests for ChargeRepository.save and get_latest (repository.py); tests/test_charge.py only covers ChargeAccount (from: Test Coverage for Complex Functions)
Check that ChargeRequest (charge.py) validates amount is positive and currency is well-formed before the gateway call (from: standard/correctness)
Check that ChargeAccount and ChargeRepository follow the same class-naming suffixes as sibling use cases and repositories in other modules (from: Naming Consistency)
Check whether the except Exception in charge.py needs a comment explaining why gateway failures are converted to None instead of raised (from: Meaningful Comments for Complex Logic)
Check that ChargeAccount.execute returning None on failure will not be confused by callers with a legitimate 'no charge' result (from: standard/correctness)
Check that ChargeRepository.get_latest (repository.py) orders its query before calling first(), since an unordered select does not return the latest charge (from: standard/correctness)
